newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 30.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- Licensing Macintosh clones was the first, most visible move in Apple Computer's step to overhaul itself after years of fitful financial performance.
- Norfolk Southern has asked a federal agency to overhaul a provision in Conrail's merger deal with CSX that prohibits Conrail from seeking another merger partner before 1999.
- Lucent Technologies and Northern Telecom are investing hundreds of millions of dollars to make wireless handsets.
- In the looming market for wireless handsets, makers of a new type of chip made from gallium arsenide stand to benefit.
- Public safety agencies are complaining that the communications revolution is imperilling their ability to maintain viable emergency frequencies.

- Amid complaints from some that advertising rates are higher and coverage is less thorough, the circulation of the Houston Chronicle has grown since the newspaper bought its rival, the Houston Post, and shut it.

- In a number of radio markets around the country, a single owner may own from three to five stations and as a result many listeners are finding themselves with fewer local news sources as news staffs are combined.
- The proliferation of corporate sites on the World Wide Web sometimes obscures the fact that it was homegrown sites that drove much of the Web's early success.
- Television viewer advocacy groups in 1996 have seen some success in holding broadcasters accountable for programming decisions.

- In the last few years, Canada and Mexico developed large markets in which otherwise law-abiding consumers openly bought and installed satellite dishes and subscribed to pirated services available due to satellite signals spilling over national borders.
